scope: Normal GLM, GPT and Gemini profile/carry repairs; only GLM also has a fallen repair. Existing tainted recolors inherit geometry, not the newly approved tainted identities. Offline only.

sources.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: original pixel-art game animation parts sheet for NORMAL GLM-chan, not the white-haired tainted design. Image 1 is the approved black-haired, black/white fox-maid costume reference. Image 2 is her current game atlas, a style and scale reference only.
Create ONE transparent landscape sheet arranged as exactly three equally spaced columns and two equally spaced rows, six clearly separated pieces with generous transparent gutters. Each piece is a tiny squat chibi BODY COMPONENT FROM COLLAR TO SHOES, with no head, face, ears or hair: the game draws its head on another layer. No neck stump or anatomical detail, just a closed costume collar.
All six body pieces are in a genuine strict RIGHT SIDE PROFILE, not a narrowed front view. Show the nearer white sleeve, black bodice, white skirt panel beneath the black outer dress, small dark boots, and a restrained black fox tail with white tip behind the torso. Stubby rounded proportions, simplified readable silhouette, crisp large pixel clusters, dark outline and a small flat-color palette; no painterly gradients, blur or adult realistic anatomy.
Top row: three successive rightward walking phases: left foot forward, feet passing, right foot forward; arms naturally at sides. Bottom row: the corresponding same three walking phases with both short arms raised above the collar to carry an item above the separate head layer. Do not draw the carried item. All body parts keep the same size, shoulder position and ground baseline in their own cell. Feet fully visible and never joined into a single leg. Every figure complete within its cell. No grid lines, numbers, captions, logo, background or extra poses. Actual transparent RGBA. Noncommercial derivative credited to ZipZipPipe. Draw only these requested original costume parts; do not reproduce any extracted vanilla artwork.

Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: one original pixel-art complete fallen/death pose for NORMAL GLM-chan in an Isaac mod. Image 1 is the exact normal costume/identity reference; Image 2 supplies the existing chibi game-sprite face and proportions.
Draw one tiny, cute, non-graphic chibi character lying completely on her side on the ground, head toward the LEFT and boots toward the RIGHT. The torso is HORIZONTAL and rests on the ground, not seated, kneeling or upright. Her large rounded head, small clothed torso and both legs form one readable reclining silhouette. Eyes softly closed, both arms relaxed beside her small closed dark book. No injury, blood or violent detail.
Preserve NORMAL GLM-chan's black hair with a few pale ends, fox ears, black/white frilled headpiece, pale face, black/white dress and fluffy black tail with a white tip. Simplify into crisp chunky pixel-art clusters with a dark outline and a few flat shades, matching the game's small chibi scale. Do not make an elaborate anime illustration. Overall silhouette is wider than tall, fitting approximately a 36-by-27 logical-pixel envelope when packed, with the whole head, ears, tail and boots visible. Center the single horizontal sprite with plenty of transparent space on all sides. Actual transparent RGBA; no scene, ground shadow, glow, text, grid, logo, extra characters or extra poses. Noncommercial derivative of the credited ZipZipPipe design, no copied vanilla pixels.

fit_revision.scope: Common profile/carry scale preserves foreground face clearance; fallen source and pixels unchanged.

sources.prompt:
Edit the supplied headless costume animation sheet. Preserve the character's existing costume identity and color palette, but correct TWO production issues: excessive tiny decoration and contact phases that do not clearly exchange the nearer leg. Produce a fresh, clean TRANSPARENT RGBA 1536x1024 sheet, THREE equal columns by TWO equal rows, SIX separate headless chibi body parts, generous transparent gutters of at least 40 pixels around every part. All parts must fit their own 512x512 cell without crossing a boundary. No glow, backdrop, shadow, text or grid.

Treat every component as a small 18-pixel-high game sprite enlarged with nearest-neighbor pixels: very squat clothed torso, short legs, chunky boots, large flat clusters, one dark outline and only a few broad shades. Remove fine lace, little jewels, pattern texture, gradients and subpixel speckles. No head, neck stump, face or hair. This is a costume body layer in a tiny game, not a tall anime figure. Keep strict RIGHT side profile.

Top row walking: cell 1 NEAR LEG forward (bright boot on RIGHT), FAR LEG backward (darker boot on LEFT). Cell 2 passing: near leg straight supporting torso, far knee bent with lifted boot, feet close. Cell 3 NEAR LEG backward (bright boot on LEFT), FAR LEG forward (darker boot on RIGHT). The third cell must visibly reverse the leading leg from the first, not merely change the sleeve. Preserve one consistent torso, neckline, scale and ground baseline.
Bottom row repeats these exact three leg positions with both short arms raised to the sides of the separate head, never holding an item. Keep the same torso/boot scale as the top row. A compact tail trails to the LEFT. No additions to the costume or official logos. Noncommercial derivative credited to ZipZipPipe, no extracted vanilla art.
Keep the white/lavender dragon-girl dress, simplified flower at waist, very small folded pale wing and short curled lavender tail. Make the skirt hem compact, with two clearly visible boots. The soft pale normal palette stays unchanged.
